title: HosMo ACTIVE – Developing, Implementing, and Piloting a Hospital Mobility Concept to Increase Physical Activity During Hospital Stay
summary:
Many patients move much less than necessary during their hospital stay. This can lead to muscle loss, reduced strength, and complications such as thrombosis or pneumonia. HosMo AKTIV therefore works together with patients, nurses, physiotherapists and clinicians, as well as health insurance companies to develop a concept that facilitates and promotes mobility in hospital care. The concept will be tested in three hospitals and compared with wards receiving standard care.
HosMo AKTIV is carried out in two phases First, a hospital mobility concept is developed in collaboration with the interprofessional team. Building on existing scientific evidence, an analysis of current practice on the wards and interviews with relevant stakeholders will be conducted. The concept is then introduced into routine care over a six-month period and tested on selected wards in comparison to usual care. In parallel, the project assesses how well the strategies are adopted and implemented in routine care and what resources are required, complemented by interviews with patients. The findings will inform a step-by-step implementation handbook to help other wards and hospitals put the concept into routine practice.

interventions.name: Patients in the intervention group (6 wards, 2 per university hospital, cluster-randomised) will receive a comprehensive, multimodal programme to increase physical activity during their inpatient stay. Patients in the control group (6 wards, 2 per university hospital, cluster-randomised) will not receive strategies for increasing physical activity. They will therefore receive no additional intervention and will continue to receive usual inpatient care (treatment as usual).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Sufficient German language proficiency to provide legally valid informed consent
- Planned minimum hospital length of stay of at least 3 days
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients who have already been diagnosed with pneumonia and/or thrombosis at the time of hospital admission
- Patients admitted to intensive care, palliative care, psychiatric, or psychosomatic wards.
